name: Dickens Special
description: Characters and places from the novels of Charles Dickens.

words.fagin: The receiver of stolen goods who runs a gang of child pickpockets in Oliver Twist.
words.sikes: Bill Sikes, the violent housebreaker in Oliver Twist.
words.nancy: Sikes's companion in Oliver Twist, who risks everything to help Oliver.
words.twist: Oliver Twist, the workhouse orphan who asks for more.
words.monks: Oliver's scheming half-brother in Oliver Twist.
words.bates: Charley Bates, one of Fagin's young pickpockets in Oliver Twist.
words.giles: Mr Giles, the Maylies' butler who shoots Oliver during the burglary.
words.belle: The young woman Scrooge once loved, seen in A Christmas Carol.
words.peter: Peter Cratchit, proudly wearing his father's shirt collar in A Christmas Carol.
words.carol: A Christmas Carol, Dickens's 1843 ghost story.
words.biddy: Pip's kind, clever friend in Great Expectations.
words.trabb: The tailor in Great Expectations, whose boy mocks Pip in the street.
words.satis: Satis House, Miss Havisham's decaying home in Great Expectations.
words.uriah: Uriah Heep, the 'umble schemer in David Copperfield.
words.agnes: Agnes Wickfield, David's steady friend and later his wife in David Copperfield.
words.clara: The name of both David Copperfield's mother and his nurse, Peggotty.
words.janet: Betsey Trotwood's maid, sent out to chase donkeys off the green.
words.salem: Salem House, Mr Creakle's harsh school in David Copperfield.
words.joram: Of Omer and Joram, the Yarmouth undertakers in David Copperfield.
words.dover: Where young David Copperfield walks to find his aunt, Betsey Trotwood.
words.quilp: Daniel Quilp, the malicious moneylender in The Old Curiosity Shop.
words.trent: Little Nell's surname in The Old Curiosity Shop.
words.smike: The ill-treated boy Nicholas rescues from Dotheboys Hall in Nicholas Nickleby.
words.ralph: Ralph Nickleby, Nicholas's cold, money-lending uncle.
words.noggs: Newman Noggs, Ralph Nickleby's downtrodden but loyal clerk.
words.gride: Arthur Gride, the old miser who plans to marry Madeline Bray in Nicholas Nickleby.
words.fanny: Fanny Squeers in Nicholas Nickleby, and Fanny Dorrit in Little Dorrit.
words.greta: Greta Bridge, the Yorkshire coaching stop on the road to Dotheboys Hall.
words.bowes: The Yorkshire village whose real boarding school inspired Dotheboys Hall.
words.toots: Mr Toots, the kind, awkward young man in Dombey and Son.
words.gills: Solomon Gills, keeper of the Wooden Midshipman shop in Dombey and Son.
words.flora: Flora Finching, Arthur Clennam's chattering old flame in Little Dorrit.
words.casby: Christopher Casby, the kindly-looking but grasping landlord in Little Dorrit.
words.gowan: Henry Gowan, the idle artist who marries Pet Meagles in Little Dorrit.
words.doyce: Daniel Doyce, the inventor and Arthur Clennam's partner in Little Dorrit.
words.krook: The rag-and-bottle dealer in Bleak House who dies of spontaneous combustion.
words.guppy: Mr Guppy, the lawyer's clerk who proposes to Esther in Bleak House.
words.flite: Miss Flite, who haunts the Court of Chancery with her caged birds in Bleak House.
words.kenge: 'Conversation' Kenge, the Jarndyce family's lawyer in Bleak House.
words.squod: Phil Squod, Trooper George's loyal helper in Bleak House.
words.clare: Ada Clare, one of the wards of Jarndyce in Bleak House.
words.sissy: Sissy Jupe, the circus girl taken in by Mr Gradgrind in Hard Times.
words.lorry: Jarvis Lorry, the Tellson's Bank man in A Tale of Two Cities.
words.pross: Miss Pross, Lucie Manette's fierce companion in A Tale of Two Cities.
words.lucie: Lucie Manette, the golden thread of A Tale of Two Cities.
words.paris: The second of A Tale of Two Cities, alongside London.
words.rudge: Barnaby Rudge, the simple young man with a raven named Grip.
words.dolly: Dolly Varden, the locksmith's flirtatious daughter in Barnaby Rudge.
words.miggs: Miss Miggs, the Vardens' sour servant in Barnaby Rudge.
words.stagg: The blind man who keeps the 'Prentice Knights' cellar in Barnaby Rudge.
words.jonas: Jonas Chuzzlewit, the brutal villain of Martin Chuzzlewit.
words.slyme: Chevy Slyme, a sponging Chuzzlewit relation.
words.hexam: Lizzie Hexam, the waterman's daughter in Our Mutual Friend.
words.venus: Mr Venus, the taxidermist and bone articulator in Our Mutual Friend.
words.jenny: Jenny Wren, the dolls' dressmaker in Our Mutual Friend.
words.bella: Bella Wilfer, the spirited heroine of Our Mutual Friend.
words.betty: Betty Higden, the old woman who dreads the workhouse in Our Mutual Friend.
words.drood: Edwin Drood, whose disappearance is Dickens's unfinished mystery.
words.edwin: The young man at the heart of The Mystery of Edwin Drood.
